title: The Shape in the Doorway
description: You reach the far end of the hall. The door ahead is open — has been open, you think, for a very long time. Something fills the lower half of the frame. It takes a moment to understand what you are seeing: a figure, collapsed face-down across the threshold, limbs at angles that suggest it did not fall so much as stop. The door cannot close around it. Neither can you pass without stepping over.

choices.label: Step over quickly and move on
choices.description: Cross the threshold in one motion, eyes forward.

success.narrative: Your foot clears it cleanly and you are through before you can think too carefully about what your boot grazed.

failure.narrative: Your foot catches on something — an arm, a wrist — and the floor comes up hard to meet your hands.

choices.label: Crouch and examine it before crossing
choices.description: Get low. Look at what is actually there before you commit.

success.narrative: You see enough to know it will not move, and you step over it with steady hands.

failure.narrative: Crouching brings your face too close; the detail is wrong in ways you cannot name and cannot unsee.

choices.label: Drag it clear of the doorway first
choices.description: Move it aside before you cross — you will not leave your back exposed to something you stepped over.

success.narrative: It moves. It is heavier than it should be and lighter than you feared, and you do not let yourself think about the difference.

failure.narrative: Halfway through, your grip fails — or something resists — and the shape tilts toward you; you wrench away and stumble through regardless, shaking.

visual.alt_text: A dim doorway at the end of a stone corridor, its door hanging open on rusted hinges. A figure lies collapsed across the threshold, face down, limbs splayed at wrong angles.
